title: New Tax Regime: Deductions & Exemptions You Can No Longer Claim
description: The new income tax regime, now the default, offers lower tax rates but requires taxpayers to forego most common deductions and exemptions. Taxpayers still ret.

faq.q: What is the main difference between the old and new tax regimes?
faq.a: The old tax regime has higher tax rates but allows numerous deductions and exemptions (like 80C, HRA, home loan interest). The new tax regime offers lower tax rates but eliminates most of these deductions, making tax calculation simpler.

faq.q: Is the new tax regime mandatory?
faq.a: No, the new tax regime is the default from FY 2023-24, meaning it applies automatically if you don't choose. However, salaried individuals and pensioners can still opt for the old regime annually when filing their Income Tax Return.

faq.q: Which deductions are still available under the new tax regime?
faq.a: Under the new tax regime, you can still claim the standard deduction of ₹50,000 for salaried individuals and pensioners, and the employer's contribution to NPS under Section 80CCD(2). Agricultural income also remains exempt.

faq.q: Can I switch between regimes every year?
faq.a: Yes, salaried individuals and pensioners have the flexibility to choose between the old and new tax regimes every financial year when filing their ITR. Individuals with business income, however, can only switch once in their lifetime.

faq.q: How do I inform my employer about my chosen tax regime?
faq.a: Your employer will typically ask you to declare your preferred tax regime at the beginning of the financial year or during specific periods. This declaration impacts your monthly TDS. If you don't declare, the new regime will be applied by default.

faq.q: Does the new tax regime affect capital gains tax?
faq.a: No, the new tax regime primarily impacts income tax on salary, business income, and other income sources. Capital gains tax provisions and rates remain the same regardless of which income tax regime you choose.

faq.q: Is the standard deduction available in the new tax regime?
faq.a: Yes, from Financial Year 2023-24 (Assessment Year 2024-25) onwards, a standard deduction of ₹50,000 is available for salaried individuals and pensioners under the new tax regime.
